Add todo, deadline and event task types for Level 4
Refactor task types into Todo, Deadline and Event
commitResults.messageBody:
This commit assigns each type its own subclass of Task so it only holds the
fields it needs and knows how to display itself. EV then stores them all
through references to Task, such that the storage, listing and marking code
no longer needs change when a new type is added.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle invalid user input
Refactor input validation to use EVException
commitResults.messageBody: Throws a checked EVException from the point each problem is detected and catch it once in the command loop. This causes the compiler to now enforce the handling that was previously left to the caller, and isolates the decision of how to errors are displayed to the user in one place.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete command
Replace task array with ArrayList
commitResults.messageBody:
Before this, the fixed array forces a manual shift on delete, a separate taskCount that can drift and a MAX_TASKS limit to check before every addition.

Storing tasks in an ArrayList is a better choice, since it resizes itself and reports its own size. This removes the shift loop, the counter, the capacity constant and the error when the registry is full.

commitResults.messageTitle: Used an enum for commands
commitResults.messageBody:
The Command enum maps each keyword to a constant, and
rejects unknown words up front. This ensures that the compiler now checks every command reference, and the fall-through error at the end of the loop is gone.

commitResults.messageBody:
Checkstyle enforces only part of the Java coding standard this course
requires. Rules such as American spelling in comments, whether a
boolean name reads like a boolean, and whether associated constants
share a common prefix are checked only by human reviewers, in peer PR
reviews and in the Practical Exam.

Nothing in the repository recorded those rules, so they had to be
looked up on the SE-EDU site each time or recalled from memory. Both
are error-prone: a peer review earlier this week cited a test-naming
rule that turned out to permit the very form it flagged.

Let's capture both standards as skills:

* seedu-java-coding-standard covers the basic and intermediate Java
  rules, and notes which of them Checkstyle cannot see
* seedu-git-standard covers commit message subject and body
  conventions, and branch naming

Both are written from the SE-EDU source pages rather than adapted from
another student's repository, so no reuse attribution is required.

commitResults.messageTitle: Point AGENTS.md at the new standard skills
commitResults.messageBody:
AGENTS.md referenced the SE-EDU Java conventions index page, which does
not say which rule levels apply. This course requires the basic and
intermediate levels specifically.

The student profile fields were also still template placeholders, so
they gave no guidance on how much explanation is useful or what to
skip.

Let's point the coding standards section at the intermediate page and
at the two new skills, fill in the profile, and add a testing policy so
coverage expectations are recorded alongside the rest.

commitResults.messageTitle: Upgrade Checkstyle to 14.1.0
commitResults.messageBody:
Checkstyle 11.0.0 predates JDK 25 and cannot parse some of the
language constructs the project now compiles against, so the
checkstyleMain task was at risk of failing on valid source.

Version 14.1.0 is the first release with full Java 25 grammar
support, which keeps the style gate meaningful rather than
silently skipped.

commitResults.messageTitle: Search task descriptions rather than rendered text
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList.find matched against Task.toString(), which includes the
status icon and type tag. Searching for "X" therefore returned
every completed task, and "[T" returned every todo.

Adding Task.getDescription() lets find match only what the user
actually typed. Deadlines and events are no longer findable by
their formatted date, which matches what the method's Javadoc
already promised. The TaskList(ArrayList) constructor now copies
its argument so callers cannot mutate the registry from outside.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove duplication and magic values
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui.getList and Ui.getFound were identical apart from their header
line; both now delegate to one private formatter. EV.getGreeting
called ui.getWelcome() twice on the same path and now calls it
once.

The data file path and the date pattern were literals buried in
method bodies and are now named constants, with the
DateTimeFormatter built once at class level instead of on every
parse.

EV.execute returned an empty string for unrecognized commands,
which would silently do nothing for any enum value added to
Command but not wired into the switch. It now throws.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #1 from aerodart/branch-A-CodeQuality
commitResults.messageBody: Improve code quality across UI, parser and task registry

commitResults.messageTitle: Correct find description in the user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
The guide said find matches a task's text, which was accurate when
find filtered on Task.toString(). It now matches the description
only, so the guide overstated what a search will return.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add sort command for the task registry
commitResults.messageBody:
Users could list tasks only in insertion order, which gets hard to
scan once the registry holds more than a handful of entries.

The sort command returns an alphabetically ordered view and leaves
the stored order untouched, so saving after a sort does not rewrite
the data file into a new order the user did not ask for.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #2 from aerodart/branch-BCD-Extension
commitResults.messageBody: Add sort command for the task registry

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep valid tasks when the data file has a damaged line
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage.load aborted on the first line it could not decode, so EV fell
back to an empty registry. The next command then saved that empty
registry over the file, destroying every valid task. A file with three
good entries and one bad one was reduced to zero bytes by typing list.

load now skips damaged lines and reports how many it left out, so a
single corrupt entry costs the user that entry and nothing else.

commitResults.messageTitle: Save the registry only after commands that change it
commitResults.messageBody:
getResponse saved after every command, including list, find and sort.
Two consequences: a registry that failed to load was written back over
the data file by a read-only command, and a read-only ev.txt made list
report a write error instead of listing anything.

Command now knows whether it mutates the registry, which keeps the
decision next to the command definitions rather than in a condition
EV has to maintain separately.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject dates that do not exist
commitResults.messageBody:
The input formatter used the default SMART resolver, which silently
corrected out-of-range fields instead of refusing them. 2026-02-30
was stored as Feb 28 and 2400 as the following midnight, so a user
typing a wrong date got a task on a date they never asked for and no
indication anything had changed.

STRICT rejects them instead. The pattern moves from yyyy to uuuu
because year-of-era requires an explicit era under STRICT, which
would reject every date including valid ones.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject descriptions containing the storage separator
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage encodes a task as fields joined by " | " and decodes by
splitting on the same string, so a description containing a pipe was
written out and read back truncated. "alpha | beta" came back as
"alpha" with no warning, on the next launch.

Refusing the character at parse time keeps the encoding assumption in
one place rather than escaping on write and unescaping on read.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add regression tests for strict date parsing
commitResults.messageBody:
The STRICT resolver change shipped without tests, so nothing pinned
the behaviour it introduced. These cover the two silent corrections
that motivated it, February 30 and hour 2400, plus a leap day to
prove the tighter resolver still accepts real dates.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject searches with no keyword and events that end before they start
commitResults.messageBody:
find delegated straight to String.contains, and contains("") is true
for every task, so a bare find listed the whole registry as though it
had matched. An event with /to earlier than /from was accepted and
rendered as a range running backwards.

Both are caught in Parser so EV.execute keeps dispatching only.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove blank lines before class closing braces
commitResults.messageBody:
Storage and TaskListTest were the only two files leaving a blank line
between the last member and the closing brace. The standard uses blank
lines to separate logical units within a block, and nothing follows
the last one.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ignore case when matching and ordering task descriptions
commitResults.messageBody:
find compared with String.contains, so "find book" missed a task
called "Borrow Book". sortByDescription used natural String order,
which is codepoint order, so "Zebra" sorted ahead of "apple" rather
than after "banana".

find lowercases against Locale.ENGLISH rather than the JVM default, so
a match does not depend on the locale of the machine running E.V.
CASE_INSENSITIVE_ORDER is already locale-independent, so sort needs no
such pin.

commitResults.messageTitle: Tell the user when a listing has nothing in it
commitResults.messageBody:
list, find and sort printed their header with no rows beneath it when
there was nothing to show, which reads as truncated output rather than
an empty result. An empty registry and a search that matched nothing
were indistinguishable from a rendering failure.

commitResults.messageTitle: Trim user input before parsing it
commitResults.messageBody:
Ui.readCommand trimmed console input but MainWindow passed the text
field's contents through untouched, so " list" worked in the terminal
and reported an unknown command in the GUI. Splitting on whitespace
rather than a literal space also accepts input containing tabs.

Parser now owns the normalization, so every entry point behaves the
same way.

commitResults.messageTitle: Report interface failures instead of printing stack traces
commitResults.messageBody:
Both FXML load failures called printStackTrace, which writes to a
console no GUI user sees. DialogBox then carried on to setText on a
field the failed load had left null, so the visible symptom was a
NullPointerException rather than the missing resource behind it.

Main now shows the user a dialog before exiting. DialogBox throws,
since a missing FXML file is a packaging fault with no user remedy.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-A-MoreErrorHandling'
commitResults.messageBody:
Comprises eleven commits hardening input handling and the data file. The
headline fix is that a single damaged line in ev.txt no longer
destroys every other task. load abandoned the whole file on the
first bad line and the next command then saved the resulting empty
registry over it.

The rest reject dates that do not exist, descriptions containing
the storage separator, searches with no keyword, and events that
end before they start. Searching and sorting now not case-sensitive,
input is trimmed so the GUI and console do not conflict with each other.

Interface failures now show the user a dialog rather than a stack trace
on a console not visible when the JAR is launched by double-clicking.

commitResults.messageTitle: Describe the GUI and the behaviour added this week
commitResults.messageBody:
Both READMEs still called E.V. a command-line assistant, which has
been inaccurate since the Level-10 GUI. Neither mentioned sort. The
user guide documented find, sort and saving as they behaved before
the A-MoreErrorHandling branch.

Adds a quick start for running the released jar and a command
summary table for first-time readers.
